Town Planning Act
1952-1972

                                          VARIATION OF ZONING OF TOWN
    THE Town Planning Board, by virtue of the powers conferred by
Section 7 of the Town Planning Act 1952-1972,
        and all other powers it enabling, hereby gives notice of the
variation of the zoning of the town specified in the
    column of the Schedule hereto and declares that each area
depicted in a plan as a Special Use Zone is a Special
    Use Zone for the purpose of that Act.
          The Variation in zoning is specified in the second column
of that Schedule opposite to the town specified
    in the first column as depicted in the plan or plans specified
in the third column.
          Plans specified in this notice are available for inspection
at the Department of Lands, Surveys and Mines,
    \Vaigani, and at the office or offices specified in the fourth
column.
          A person aggrieved by or who wishes to object to the
division of a town into zones by this notice, may within
    three (3) months, after the date of the publication in the
Government Gazette of this notice, appeal to the
    Minister of the House of Assembly for Lands.

A Proclamation to delimit the offshore area.

delimit the offshore area either in whole or in

accordance with the line of delimitation

NOTIFICATION OF SUCCESSFUL APPLICANTS-LAND BOARD No. 760 ITEM 8 AND
LAND BOARD No. 884 ITEM 5


IN accordance with the provisions of the Land Art 1962, as amended
to date, it is advised that the following application heard

  at Land Board Room, Konedobu on 10th October, 1973 was successful
and was confirmed by the Minister for Lands and Envi-

ronment on 19th March, 1974.

    C.L. 1245, C.L. 1284, C.L. 395-Regal Bakeries Port Moresby Pty
Limited, a Business Lease over Allotments 5, 6, and 7,
(Consolidated), Section 1, Hohola, City of Port Moresby, Central
District.

    The new lease shall commence on the day following the date of
acceptance of surrender of Crown Leases Volume 5, Folio

1245, Volume 16, Folio 395 and Volume 6, Folio 1284.

    And also at the Papua New Guinea Central Government Offices,
Conference Room No. 6, Waigani on 4th December, 1974
was successful and was confirmed by the Minister for lands on 27th
March, 1975.

    And that condition (E) from the recommendation of Item 8 of Land
Board Meeting No. 760 be deleted and the following in-

serted in its stead:-

    (1) No overnight or early morning deliveries shall be made from
the land.

    (2) The bakery will be effectively screened to prevent any

disturbing sounds or odours being transmitted.

    (3) Off street parking shall be provided in accordance with
Clause 2.801 of the Building Regulations 1971.

    Dated at City of Port Moresby this tenth day of April, One
thousand nine hundred and seventy-five.


A. 0. TAVIAI,


Director of Lands, Surveys and Mines.

KEROSENE
     MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller, by virtue
of the powers conferred by the Prices Reg-
    ' elation Act 1949, as amended to date, and all other powers me
enabling, do hereby make the following Order
   under that Act:—
                          PRICES ORDER No. 138
   1. CITATION.
      This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 138.
   2. COMMENCEMENT.
      This Order shall come into operation on the date of
publication of this Order in the Gazette.
   3. REVOCATION.
      The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
   4. DEFINITIONS.
      In this Order—
       "petrol", includes any substance normally sold a petrol
whether or not containing additives of any kind;
       "distillate" includes any substance normally sold a
automotive distillate whether or not containing additives
         of any kind;
       "kerosene" includes any substance normally sold a kerosene,
being a medium refined petroleum product as
         used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether
or not containing additives of any kind;
       "wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene
means a person or a firm who sells petrol, dis-
         tillate or kerosene for the purpose of resale and not for
the purpose of use;
       "supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or kerosene,
means a person or a firm who sells petrol, distillate
         or kerosene for the purpose of use;
       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
   5. MAXIMUM PRICE.

(i) Subject to Subclause (ii) of this clause, where petrol,
distillate or kerosene is supplied—
       (a) at a locality specified in the first column of Schedule 1
to this Order; or
       (b) at some other place to which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene is transported from any such locality by
         or on behalf of a wholesaler or the supplier;
   the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
kerosene may be supplied is the sum of—
       (c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the Second,
Third or Fourth Column as the case may be, of
         Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and
       (d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to
in paragraph (b) of this subclause.

LAND AVAILABLE FOR LEASING
TENDERS and/or applications, as applicable, are invited for the
right to a lease or leases over the land or lands as described
in the following advertisements on the terms and conditions as set
out and subject to the provisions of the Land Act 1962 (as
amended)
The attention of tenderer' and applicants is directed towards the
following:-
Tenders.-The upset price where shown below is the assessed
unimproved value of the land, and is the minimum amount
acceptable as a tender. Tenders may be for any amount in
excess of the upset price, but the successful tenderer will only
be required to pay the difference between the upset price and
the amount of the tender.

highest or any tender will not necessarily be accepted.
Fees.-All tenders and applications must be accompanied
by an application fee of One Kina (K1) for each, portion
or allotment required. Following the grant of a lease an
additional fee for the preparation of lease document, the
amount of tender less the upset price where applicable and,
if surveyed, the prescribed survey fee shall be payable within
two (2) months from the date of grant.
Preference.-Tenderers and applicants are advised to indicate
preferences if there are more than one allotment or portion

being advertised in any particular advertisement, but only one
registration of application fee need be lodged if only one
allotment or portion is required. If more than one allotment or
portion is required, an additional fee for each such portion or
allotment must be lodged.
Tenderers and Applicants.-Tendcrers and applicants must
state full name, occupation and postal address. If more than
one person is tendering or applying, it must be stated whether
joint tenancy or tenancy-in-common is required. If a company,
the full registered name and address of the company and that
of its representative must be stated, A business name cannot
hold land.
Improvements.-Expected development in respect of agricul-
tural leases is indicated in the respective advertisements; how-
ever, full proposals of proposed development shall be submitted
by tenderers or applicants seeking other types of leases or
larger agricultural leases unless development is specified in
detail in any particular advertisement. Where applicable devel-
opment shall comply with the requirements of the Town Plan-
ning Act and the Building Regulations.
Term of Lease.-Unless otherwise indicated each lease shall
be for a term of ninety-nine (99) years.
General condition' pertaining to Business Leases.-Provided
all other factors are equal, preference may be given to indig-
enous proposals, or proposals which contain a significant pro-
portion of indigenous equity. In the event that a lease is
recommended because of a proposal to include a significant
portion of indigenous equity, the lease shall contain a clause
requiring specific performance of that proposal within a time
specified. In all cases where a lease is granted to non-Papua
New Guineans or companies or associations not containing a
significant amount of the indigenous equity, the lease may
contain a clause requiring the lessee to achieve a specific level

Improvements.—Section 57 of the Land Act 1962-74, provides that
an Agricultural Lease shall contain conditions prescribing

the minimum improvements to be carried out by the Lessee. Conditions
applicable to the leases described above are as follows:-


      1. Of the land suitable for cultivation the following
proportions shall be planted in a good and husbandlike manner with

           a crop or crops of economic value which shall be
harvested regularly in accordance with sound commercial practice:


            (a) One-tenth in the first period of 2 years of the
term;


            (b) One-fifth in the first period of 5 years of the
term;


            and during the remainder of the term, one-fifth of the
land so suitable shall be kept so planted.


      2. That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be stocked with a minimum of 1 head of great cattle

           per 3 hectares within 5 years from date of grant, and
shall be kept so stocked to that minimum for the remainder of the

           term.


      3. That portion of the lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall within 3 years from the date of grant be fenced exter-

           nally, except in such parts of the boundaries as the
presence of natural features make this unnecessary with a barbed

           wire fence of not less than 4 strands having posts not
more than 4.5 metres (15 feet) apart, and strainer posts at

           least every 100 metres (5 chains), the said fence to be
kept well strained and in stock-proof condition.

4. That portion of the Lease which is to be utilised for
grazing shall be subdivided by fencing into at least 3 paddocks,

           within 3 years from the date of grant. Any one paddock
shall not exceed more than half of the area used for grazing.


      5. Yards and handling facilities to the satisfaction of the
Land Board shall be constructed within 3 years of the date of

             grant.


      6. Condition of improvements may, at the discretion of the
Minister for Lands upon the recommendation of the Land

           Board, be modified in accordance with the detailed
development proposals of the applicant submitted in evidence to the

             Land Board.


      7. Provided always that if at the end of the first 2 years of
the Lease it appears that reasonable efforts are not being made

           to fulfil the stocking and improvement conditions, the
Minister for Lands may, by notice in the Gazette, and in accord-

             ance with the provisions of the Land Act 1962-74 forfeit
the Lease.


        8. These Leases are reserved for Papua New Guinean applicants
only.


        Residence Condition:—The Lessee or his Agent shall take up
residency or occupancy of his block within six months from

the date of grant.


    Applicants are warned that applications must be lodged at or
posted so as to reach the Lands Department, Waigani,

before 3 p.m., Wednesday, 25th June, 1975. All applications must be
accompanied by the prescribed fee of two kina

(K2.00) for each lease required. Applications not conforming to
these requirements will be rejected as informal.

                VACANCY—CENTRAL PLANNING OFFICE
               ASSOCIATE DIRECTOR—POSITION No. C12(T)
APPLICATIONS are invited from suitably qualified persons for
selection as the Associate Director of the Central
  Planning Office.
  The salary payable will be negotiable but will be not less than
K7,365 per annum (Level 1).
  The successful applicant will undertake a programm of training
with a view to early promotion to the position
of Director of the Central Planning Office, subject to satisfactory
performance. He will be given the earliest possible
opportunity to take full responsibility for the duties of the
position.
  The duties of the Director include:
   —Direct, control, plan and co-ordinate the activities of the
Central Planning Office.
   —Advise the National Planning Committee of Cabinet and individual
Ministers on policy matters.
   —Propose integrated policies to achieve the Government's
objectives and incorporate these policies into a
      National Improvement Programme.
   —Ensure transmission of approved policy to departments and areas.
   —Oversee implementation, report on progress and recommend action.
   —Hold statutory appointments and act as a member of Councils,
Boards and Committees related to the func-
      tions of the Office.
, 'Applicants should have a good educational background desirably
including relevant tertiary qualifications;
brillOsing ability; ability to manage technical experts and
communicate to decision makers.
